In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of the 135, 000-Mr polypetide as the catalytic subunit of TPP II.
the occurrence and distribution of TPP II in mammalian erythrocytes and in other tissues.
the occurrence and characterization of TPP II in haemocytes, liver and Escherichia cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TPP II activity is present in the erythrocytes of all species tested except the hen, and that TPP II is a common enzyme in liver homogenates.
the 135, 000-Mr polypetide is a component of TPP II in the haemolysate of all species tested, except the calf.
TPP II is a widely distributed enzyme in mammalian tissues, but is absent in erythrocyte membranes of calf and hen.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TPP II is present in erythrocyte haemolysate from all the species examined, except for the calf, and in the liver of all the species tested, except for the hen.
the 135, 000-Mr polypetide is the TPP II enzyme and that the 105,000-Mr and 84, 000-M polypeptides may be degradation products of the TPP II enzyme.
TPP II is present in haemolysis of all the species examined and in homogenates from all species, but not in E. coli, whereas the activity in erythrocyte haemolysate varies considerably.
The main takeaway from our work is that
tripeptidase is a common feature of eukaryotes.
